_note: Plugins is the skill allow-list GilbertOne's tool gateway reaches: which named skills may be invoked, in which jurisdiction, behind which grant, and the shape each one's input must match. It is a DATA contract, not an engine file — it is deliberately not listed in packages/catalog/apis.json's engineFiles and declares no engine in packages/catalog/events.json, because packages/catalog/apis/ holds exactly one file per declared engine and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs refuses any other. The four routes below are therefore conceptual and every one is "proposed": they are documentation of the surface this allow-list describes, not governed engine routes, and they become real only when the founder decides whether the plugin gateway extends the access engine's tool-gateway (POST /v1/access/tools/{tool}, §15D) or becomes an engine of its own. That decision is deferred. packages/gilbertone/src/tools.ts reads this file's allow-list statically — no network, no environment — to populate its ToolRegistry, and the refusal sentences a plugin meets live here rather than in code, so the words that refuse a skill are the words the accountable people can read in advance.

jurisdictions.label: South Africa
jurisdictions.why: The only jurisdiction MyThuso is deployed in today. A skill is approved for the jurisdictions it names and refused everywhere else, so a skill nobody approved for a place is never invoked there.

_schemaFieldTypesNote: The types a plugin's declared input schema may name, kept to the field types packages/catalog/feeds.json already defines so a plugin schema speaks the same vocabulary as every route. A skill whose input does not match its declared schema is refused with plugin-schema-violation rather than invoked on a guess.

pluginStates.label: On the allow-list
pluginStates.why: The skill may be invoked in a jurisdiction it names, behind the grants it declares.

pluginStates.label: Revoked
pluginStates.why: The skill was on the allow-list and has been withdrawn. It is never invoked again; an attempt is refused with plugin-revoked, and revocation is not undone by editing this file back — a revoked skill stays listed as revoked so the refusal has something to answer.

refusals.statement: That skill is not on the allowlist for this jurisdiction.
refusals.why: A patient-facing model reaches only named skills on an allow-list (§15D), never a general-purpose one. A skill nobody wrote down is refused rather than tried.

refusals.statement: That skill is not approved for use in this jurisdiction.
refusals.why: A skill approved for one place is not approved for every place. The allow-list is scoped per jurisdiction so a skill's approval never travels further than the people who gave it.

refusals.statement: That skill has been revoked and can no longer be invoked.
refusals.why: Revocation is permanent for the version revoked. A withdrawn skill answers 410 rather than 404 so a caller who held it knows it existed and was taken away, not that it was never there.

refusals.statement: The plugin's input does not match its declared schema.
refusals.why: A skill declares the shape of its input. An input that does not match it is refused before the skill runs, because a skill invoked on arguments it did not declare is doing something nobody reviewed.

routes.summary: List every registered skill, allowlisted or revoked, with the jurisdictions and grants each one names.
List the skills allowlisted for the current jurisdiction — the registry with everything not approved here, and everything revoked, left out.
Invoke an allowlisted skill by id, with arguments matching its declared schema, and record the invocation.
Revoke a skill's allow-list entry, so it is never invoked again and a later attempt answers plugin-revoked.

_routesNote: Conceptual documentation of the surface this allow-list describes, each marked "proposed". These are not governed engine routes: they are not in packages/catalog/apis.json's engineFiles, they carry no callers, purposes, emits or capability citations, and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs's API matrix never reads them. "answersWith" names the refusals above that the route would answer, by id, so the sentences stay in one place.

plugins.name: Book a home visit
plugins.purpose: The visits on the caller's own care plan.

input.why: The service to book, an entry in packages/catalog/services.json.
Chosen by the caller, so a retry on a dropped connection is one visit and not two.

plugins.name: Find a nearby clinic
plugins.purpose: The facilities near a place the caller names.

input.why: The zone to search, an entry in packages/catalog/geography.json.

plugins.name: Nurse queue
plugins.purpose: The nurse queue, for staff who carry the grant.

revoked.why: Gilbert never gets a general-purpose record tool (§15D). A generic FHIR read in front of a model is unrestricted access with a conversation in front of it, so it was revoked and is kept listed as revoked rather than deleted, so an attempt answers plugin-revoked.
